products.name: Mermaid
products.description: Open-source JavaScript library for creating diagrams from simple, text-based syntax. Native rendering in GitHub, GitLab, Notion, and many documentation platforms. Focus on developers and documentation-in-code workflows.
products.positioning: Code-first diagram-as-code for developers; Git-friendly; natively integrated with GitHub/GitLab

products.name: Graphviz
products.description: Open-source graph visualization software from AT&T Labs. Uses DOT language for defining graphs. Primary focus on automatic layout algorithms. Legacy tool with extensive platform integration.
products.positioning: Mature graph visualization library; strong layout algorithms; industry standard for programmatic graph generation

products.name: PlantUML
products.description: Open-source UML diagramming tool. Supports extensive UML diagram types (sequence, class, use case, etc.) plus non-UML diagrams (JSON, YAML, EBNF). JavaScript rendering engine for browser-based editing.
products.positioning: Comprehensive UML specification compliance; rich icon libraries; text-based syntax for technical diagrams

products.name: D2
products.description: Modern diagram-as-code language from Terrastruct (2022+). Features advanced TALA layout engine for superior automatic positioning. Web-based editor with hybrid drag-drop and code editing. Better visual aesthetics than legacy diagram tools.
products.positioning: Modern diagram-as-code with beautiful layouts; unified syntax across diagram types; hybrid visual+code editor

products.name: Lucidchart
products.description: Premium cloud-based diagramming and visual collaboration platform. 70+ million users. AI-powered diagram generation, real-time team collaboration, extensive template library, data linking capabilities.
products.positioning: Enterprise drag-and-drop with AI intelligence; real-time collaboration; visual process and architecture documentation

products.name: draw.io
products.description: Free and open-source drag-and-drop diagramming tool. Lightweight web-based interface (diagrams.net). Offline capability, autosave, integration with Google Drive, Confluence, Jira. 15M+ monthly users.
products.positioning: Free, lightweight drag-and-drop; offline-first; integrations with Google/Confluence ecosystem; simple UX

products.name: Creately
products.description: AI-powered visual collaboration platform. Founded 2008, bootstrapped (no external funding). Smart Canvas with intelligent shapes, data linking, real-time collaboration, extensive shape library.
products.positioning: Intelligent diagramming with smart shapes; real-time team collaboration; data integration capabilities

products.name: Penrose
products.description: Academic constraint-based diagram system from CMU. Generates beautiful diagrams automatically from mathematical notation. Three-language approach (Domain/Substance/Style). Focus on mathematical and scientific visualization.
products.positioning: Automatic beautiful diagrams from mathematical notation; constraint-based layout; academic/scientific focus

products.name: Microsoft Visio
products.description: Enterprise-grade diagramming tool by Microsoft. Available as cloud (Microsoft 365) and desktop application. Extensive template library, industry standard for business/technical diagrams. Strong Microsoft ecosystem integration.
products.positioning: Industry-standard enterprise diagramming; extensive templates; Microsoft ecosystem integration; desktop-first

products.name: SmartDraw
products.description: Competing drag-and-drop diagramming tool. Cloud-based with 4,500+ templates. Automatic formatting and positioning of shapes. Cross-platform support. Affordable pricing (~$6/month).
products.positioning: Affordable drag-and-drop with automatic formatting; template-heavy; SMB-focused alternative to Lucidchart/Visio

products.name: EdrawMax
products.description: Comprehensive diagramming tool by Wondershare. 280+ diagram types, 50,000+ symbols. Cross-platform (Windows, Mac, Linux, web). Subscriptions and perpetual licenses available. Strong export capabilities.
products.positioning: Versatile diagramming with massive symbol library; flexible licensing; cross-platform presence

competitors.wedge_vs_them: MetroGraph offers superior manual layout control and visual precision for complex database/graph schemas vs Mermaid's fixed automatic layouts; MetroGraph's hybrid UI+code approach bridges Mermaid's gap between code-first and visual needs
competitors.moat: Native GitHub rendering; 85K+ GitHub stars; massive developer adoption for documentation; simple Markdown-like syntax lowers barrier to entry

competitors.wedge_vs_them: MetroGraph provides interactive UI on top of Graphviz-class layout algorithms; targets users who want programmatic graph generation with visual precision and real-time editing vs CLI-only tool
competitors.moat: Mature layout engine; extensive platform integrations; proven reliability; AT&T Labs heritage and community trust

competitors.wedge_vs_them: MetroGraph wins on visual fluidity and layout control for non-UML diagrams (ERD, architecture); PlantUML's strength is strict UML specification compliance, MetroGraph targets database/data engineers with graph visualization needs
we_win_on: better layout control for non-UML diagrams
competitors.moat: Comprehensive UML specification support; rich visual library; strong IntelliJ IDE integration

competitors.wedge_vs_them: D2 is closest competitor: modern code-first with TALA layout and web editor. MetroGraph differentiates on database-schema focus, real-time collaboration, and metro-map-specific orthogonal layout optimizations vs D2's general-purpose diagram tool
they_win_on: modern web editor with code-visual hybrid
competitors.moat: TALA layout engine; proprietary language design; first-mover in modern diagram-as-code; brand positioning

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Lucidchart owns drag-and-drop ease and AI features for non-technical teams. MetroGraph differentiates by serving data engineers/technical users who need code-first with visual precision; Metro maps and graph-specific features vs Lucidchart's general diagramming
they_win_on: ease of use for non-technical users
competitors.moat: $1B+ valuation; 70M users; strong network effects; AI feature integration; Lucidpress ecosystem

competitors.wedge_vs_them: draw.io is free/open-source alternative to Lucidchart. MetroGraph competes on code-first and graph specialization; draw.io lacks version control and code export, ideal for quick diagrams not technical documentation
competitors.moat: Free and open-source; broad platform integrations; simplicity and lightweight design

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Creately competes on smart shapes and data linking for business users. MetroGraph targets developers/data engineers with code-first approaches; Creately's strength is visual collaboration and smart formatting for non-technical teams
competitors.moat: Smart Canvas technology; data linking; real-time collaboration; bootstrapped profitability

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Penrose is niche academic tool for mathematical notation to diagrams. MetroGraph targets practitioners with data/database schemas; Penrose is research-stage, small community, not suitable for business/engineering workflows
competitors.moat: CMU academic backing; constraint-based synthesis; ACM/SIGGRAPH publications; unique mathematical approach

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Visio is enterprise standard but expensive and collaboration-limited. MetroGraph differentiates on modern cloud-based UX, real-time collaboration, and code-first approach vs Visio's desktop/legacy paradigm
competitors.moat: Enterprise adoption; extensive templates; Microsoft integration; market positioning

competitors.wedge_vs_them: SmartDraw is affordable drag-and-drop alternative to Lucidchart/Visio. MetroGraph wins on code-first and technical workflows; SmartDraw targets SMBs wanting simple visual diagramming without technical features
competitors.moat: Affordable pricing; template library; market positioning

competitors.wedge_vs_them: EdrawMax is versatile all-purpose tool with massive symbol library. MetroGraph differentiates on database/graph specialization and code-first approach; EdrawMax is generalist with weak collaboration and no code support
competitors.moat: Massive symbol library; cross-platform presence; flexible licensing model

notes:
**Evidence Summary:**
Sources analyzed: 52 primary sources covering official homepages, documentation, GitHub repos, user reviews (Capterra/G2/TrustRadius), funding/analyst coverage, and practitioner comparison articles.

**Key Market Segments Identified:**
1. Diagram-as-code (text-first): Mermaid, Graphviz, PlantUML, D2, Penrose
2. Drag-and-drop SaaS: Lucidchart, Creately
3. Drag-and-drop free/open: draw.io
4. Enterprise/legacy: Visio, SmartDraw, EdrawMax

**Competitive Positioning vs MetroGraph:**
MetroGraph's wedge (metro-map-style node/edge graph tool addressing HCI failure of RAG/workflow/agent tools) most directly competes with:
- **High threat:** Mermaid (adoption, simplicity), D2 (modern approach, TALA layout), Lucidchart (AI + collaboration)
- **Medium threat:** Graphviz (layout quality), PlantUML (UML depth), draw.io (free alternative), Creately (smart shapes), Visio (enterprise)
- **Low threat:** Penrose (niche academic), SmartDraw (SMB-focused), EdrawMax (generalist)

**Feature Differentiation Rationale:**
Selected features emphasize:
- Canvas/visual interaction (where diagram-as-code tools are weak)
- Layout algorithms (core differentiator across tools)
- Collaboration (weak for code-first tools)
- Git/version control (strong for code-first, weak for drag-drop)
- AI assist (emerging feature, Lucidchart leads)
- ERD/schema support (relevant for ICP of noSQL/SQL data engineers)
- Templates/onboarding (maturity signal)

**Data Quality Notes:**
- All products covered in leaf scope per sources.json (9 primary + 3 related)
- Company mappings verified against market.companies; 3 new stubs created (JGraph Ltd for draw.io, SmartDraw Inc., Wondershare)
- Feature selection spans 20 of 110 available features (15-35 most relevant per instructions)
- Source citation includes T0 (primary), T1 (official), T2 (analyst), and T3 (practitioner) sources per sources.json methodology
